panel.summary: Falling back to `image/png` for an unknown/empty blob MIME can embed mislabeled image bytes in the pptx
panel.evidence: `mime: blob.type || "image/png"` — when the backend/S3 returns `application/octet-stream` (image.service.ts:121 explicitly falls back to that when S3 has no ContentType) or the fetch yields an empty type, the mime is a non-image string or forced to png. `extFromMime` in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:82-98 also defaults unknown mimes to `png`, so JPEG/GIF bytes get written as `ppt/media/imageN.png` and declared `image/png` via the [Content_Types].xml Default (templates.ts:24). PowerPoint can refuse to render such a mislabeled part. Sniffing the bytes or passing the real content type through would avoid it.
panel.finding_key: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/pptx-actions.ts::falling back to `image/png` for an unknown/empty blob mime can embed mislabeled image bytes in the pptx
